beats.t: The four were dragged in a line. The black sun drew close enough to fill the sky. Wind blew from its rim, without heat.
Yeoni, let go. Please.
No. The harder it pulls, the tighter I'll hold.
But the harder they pulled, the farther they were dragged. The black hand was eating Yeoni's strength too. Their pull became its power.
Yeoni, that won't work! It eats the force of pulling!
Then what? Let go?
Then a very old phrase returned. Yeoni couldn't remember who had said it. On the island, before the first ring.
(Don't pull. Push.)
Yeoni relaxed the hand pulling Seo Hanbi. Instead, they placed their left palm against her wrist, between the black fingers and the scar. The palm leaking gold.
Hanbi, take this. Don't repay it.
Gold pushed from Yeoni's palm into Seo Hanbi's wrist. The moment it touched the black fingers, they split cleanly, as though cut by a blade.
Ghh.
Seo Hanbi's wrist came free. The four tumbled onto a black panel. The umbrella rolled until Moka's foot stopped it.
Alive. Are we alive? How many fingers does everyone have? Count them.
Ten. Still ten for me too. One's a little black.
The black sun retreated briefly, like a beast withdrawing an injured hand. They used the opening to gather on the widest panel.
Yeoni opened their left hand. The gold was fainter than before, no more than a small ember.
It's smaller. By the amount I pushed into Hanbi.
Because of me, the piece is this small.
No. I chose. And it worked. You're here now.
Seo Hanbi held her right wrist instead of answering. The scar was warm, a temperature she had never felt there before. Moisture beaded where Metal had passed.
Wait. Seo Hanbi, let me see that wrist.
Yundal examined it. A droplet above the scar glittered with gold. He gave a short laugh.
That's it. What you just did, Yeoni—that's the answer.
Meaning? Simple words. I'm on fire duty, not thinking duty.
The five elements generate one another. Wood makes Fire, Fire makes Earth, Earth makes Metal, Metal makes Water, and Water returns to nourish Wood.
[ Wood → Fire → Earth → Metal → Water → Wood ]
Your Metal just entered Seo Hanbi and became Water. Metal generates Water. Mr. Cat's energy gave birth to rain.
My rain came from Mr. Cat.
That's the natural order. You're a summer tree, Yeoni, so your chart needs Water. That Water comes from Metal. Mr. Cat was always the one who brought rain.
(Is that why the cat always carried an umbrella? When he was human.)
Yeoni startled at their own thought. An umbrella when human? They had no memory of seeing that. Yet the note said it: Umbrella when human.
So make a circuit. Five of us holding hands, each pushing energy to the next. Not pulling.
Then the order matters. Who stands beside whom?
Like a compatibility reading. This one is free.
Yundal drew a circle on the black panel with his finger and assigned a person to each of five positions.
Yeoni is Wood. A vine, so first. Moka is Fire, on Yeoni's right.
Wood feeds me, right? Yeoni, raise me well. Expensively.
I'm Earth. After Fire. The Void is Earth, empty ground that can hold anything.
Then since I'm Water...
Seo Hanbi comes after Metal, to Yeoni's left. The problem is Metal's place.
The fifth place stood empty, between Yundal and Seo Hanbi. No one occupied it.
The cat's place.
Yes. That's why I brought this.
Yundal removed his glove. A golden thread hung at the Void's rim: the light he had caught when Neo disappeared at the tower.
The only useful thing this hand has eaten. Good thing I didn't throw it away.
You've kept it all this time?
I couldn't just throw away a clue that might bring someone else's husband back.
He's not my husband! Yet!
Yet?
Yeoni blushed. They had no idea why they'd said yet. Seo Hanbi laughed softly. This time, not just a shoulder shake, but a sound.
After the circle was drawn, no one spoke for a moment. Far away, the black sun caught its breath.
Yundal. That clock earlier. Did you really not regret leaving it?
Of course I did. Five twenty. Seeing the hands there took my breath away.
But if I received it from Black Moon, I'd spend my life as someone who borrowed time from it. I didn't want that.
Borrowed things grow. I know that well.
If the ledger expert says so, it must be true.
What will you do when you get home, Yundal?
Call my mother. See whether she remembers my voice. If not, I'll introduce myself again.
Yundal smiled, but his gloved hand was clenched. Yeoni rested a hand briefly over that fist, then lifted it.
She'll remember. We remember you. Your mother will too.
What are you plotting?
The black sun approached again. This time not its hands, but the sun itself descended. All five eyes fixed on Yeoni.
Now. Hold hands!
Five formed a circle: Yeoni, Moka, Yundal, the golden thread in the empty place, Seo Hanbi. Yundal set the thread afloat, and it stretched taut in midair.
Moka, take it!
Yeoni drew a deep breath and pushed it into Moka's hand. Vines spread across the back of their hand. Fire bloomed in Moka's palm, far larger than a match flame.
Whoa, what's this? Feels like I've got firewood!
Moka pushed the fire toward Yundal. As it touched his palm, the rim of the black circle hardened like fired clay.
Hot. But for the first time, my hand doesn't feel empty.
Yundal added Earth's energy to the golden thread. One strand split into many, tracing shoulders and hands in the empty place.
Neo's shape stood there briefly. Only a faceless golden outline. It turned toward Seo Hanbi and breathed out.
Received. Yeoni, my turn to give.
Rain poured from Seo Hanbi's umbrella. Not cold rain. It fell onto Yeoni's head, shoulders, left palm. Beneath it, the faded gold brightened again.
It went around. A full circuit!
A circle. Break it in one place, and it ends.
A black hand slipped behind Yundal. The Void suddenly gaped wide. Earth's energy began leaking from his hand.
Ah. This is a little...
You don't touch someone standing beside me!
Moka gripped Yundal's hand tighter. Fire wrapped the Earth as though firing it again. Yundal's palm hardened once more.
The five energies began circling. One turn, two. Faster each time. A bright five-pointed star formed on the black panel.
Stop. That is not something a vessel can do.
I told you, I'm not a vessel. I'm Lee Yeoni. A university student. I write star reviews and I'm bad at matching socks.
The star flew into the center of the black sun, where Sun and Moon overlapped. Cracks split the overlapping rims. Ancient light leaked through.
It's splitting! Splitting open!
Something's shining inside. Something tiny.
White. Something white.
The overlap is coming apart. But it won't hold long. It's closing again.
The split was barely wide enough for one person. Deep inside, something white flickered faintly, no larger than a firefly.
Yeoni looked at that light. Still no name came. But their feet moved toward the gap first.
You can't go alone. That's a mouth waiting to eat the vessel.
I know. But only a vessel can go in there, right? If I'm a vessel, that can be useful too.
Once you enter, I'll hold the entrance with the Void. Not for long. One song at most.
Then I'll sing. Come out before it ends. No encore.
Seo Hanbi placed the umbrella in Yeoni's hand. The handle with three layers of tape.
Take it. It's a loan. You must come back to repay it.
You just used your ledger voice.
Just this once.
Umbrella in hand, Yeoni jumped through the gap. Behind them, Moka's dreadful rap began. It grew fainter.
As they fell, sounds went out one by one. Rap, rain, their own breath. Only the umbrella handle in their hand was warm.
(When scared, notes. Going to find him. Even without remembering. Trust my handwriting.)
Inside was deep and still. Neo lay on his side on the floor. His glass-transparent body moved slowly. He opened his eyes.
“Who are you?”
I'm not quite sure either. But I came to find you. That's what my note says.
